subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Nuclear Fusion: The 30-Year Promise
description: One-minute skill: Nuclear Fusion: The 30-Year Promise.

hook.text: Fusion powers the sun. If we could replicate it on Earth, a glass of seawater could produce energy equal to a barrel of oil.

buildup.text: Fusion heats hydrogen isotopes to 150 million degrees — ten times hotter than the sun's core. At that temperature, atoms merge.

discovery.text: Tokamaks use powerful magnets to confine plasma in a doughnut shape. No physical container can survive contact with fusion plasma.

twist.text: ITER, the largest fusion experiment, has been under construction since 2010. It's years behind schedule and billions over budget.

climax.text: In 2022, the NIF achieved ignition — fusion produced more energy than the lasers put in. A milestone after decades of effort.

punchline.text: Always 30 years away. Until it wasn't. Ignition was achieved.

quiz.question: What milestone did the National Ignition Facility achieve in 2022?
options: They sustained a fusion reaction for over 24 hours continuously
Fusion produced more energy than the lasers used to initiate it
They created a tokamak small enough to fit inside a shipping container
